main_text.p: cap. ii. Ergo Marcion Cerdoni succede-re potuit circa annum CXLV. & Marcio-nis meminisse Iustinum anno CLII. Rem autem ita se habere liquet ex Epiphanio Hær. 42. ubi narrat Marcionem ob vitia-tam Virginem Ecclesiâ ab ipso Parente Sinopes Episcopo pulsum, Romam se contulisse, & cùm à Presbyteris qui Ecclesiam Romanam vacante Sede post Hy-gini mortem administrabant, in commu-nionem non admitteretur, Hæresim ar-chitectatus est, Cerdonis vestigiis insi-stens, quod circa annum Christi CXLV. ut mox dicebamus contigit. Hæc adeò clara sunt ut satis mirari nequeam, doctis-simum Vindiciarum Auctorem affirmare esse aufum pag. 81. vel saltem ut rem ma-ximè probabilem statuere; Cerdonem si non antè, ipso tamen statim initio Hadriani sua deliria disseminâsse, ut hinc concluderet Valentinum, quem Cerdone antiquiorem supponit, sua spargere po-tuisse ante undecimum annum Traiani, eáque ab Ignatio ante martyrium potuis-se cognosci. Nam contrarium planè con-stat ex ijs omnibus quæ hactenus scripsi-mus, necnon ex Veterum omnium testi-monijs, qui Cerdonem viginti quinque annis plus minus juniorem faciunt, Va-lentinum vero circiter triginta quatuor,

page.notes: A dark ink blob stands in the right margin beside the line "Rem"; it is a stain, not a note. Another blob sits at the top right corner of the scan and a dark spot at the lower left; these are scan artefacts. Between "pulsum" and "Romam" there is a small printed mark (possibly a reference or comma-like sign) that I could not identify with certainty; I transcribed it as a comma. The word "si" after "Cerdonem" may carry a ligature; read as "si". The digitiser's "Digitized by Google" line at the bottom right was omitted.
